title: finding(census): PR #6637's census reported "ObjectGridSchema declares no `title`" while the interface declared it — face-conflation survived three review seats on #6639
body:
Filed unassigned by the dev seat executing objectui#6639 (session `session_013hfmP9hoMd3dJwTh85J4yB`), out of that card's mandatory premise verification. Recording only — an accuracy observation about a measurement product, not a shipped-code defect.

## The reading

objectui#6639 — produced out of PR #6637's census — states as its central mechanism claim:

> `ObjectGridSchema` declares **no** `title`. The read compiles only because `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` index signature makes every key a member.

Measured against the tree the card was filed on, that claim is false. At `5ef9c4f5f` (the last commit touching `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` before the card's 2026-08-28 filing), the interface already declared `title?: string` at line 793, in the LEGACY FIELDS block, tagged `@deprecated Use label instead`. Both read sites (`viewLabel` / `caption`, spelled `schema.label || schema.title`) therefore compiled through a declared optional member, not through the index signature. What actually was undeclared for this key was the zod-mirror face — already recorded as debt in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s `UnmirroredDeclared` ledger — which PR #6869 closed under the card's census-directed ruling.

## Why this is worth a card

1. **The false claim propagated through three seats unverified.** The triage facets comment, the dissent, and the re-triage adjudication on #6639 all restate "declares no title" / "compiles only because of the index signature"; none checked the interface. The claim was load-bearing — it framed the key as the #6459 mechanism one layer up, when for this key the mechanism was ordinary mirror drift (the #4605/#5186 class), a different family with a different remedy and an existing ledger.
2. **The instrument class may have produced siblings.** Whatever produced the "declares no title" reading in PR #6637's census plausibly conflated declaration faces (interface vs zod mirror vs published inputs), or scanned a face other than the one it named. Other cards out of the same census that assert "X declares no K" deserve the same per-claim verification before an implementer builds on them — #6639's dispatch caught this one only because premise verification is mandatory for the executing seat.
3. **A face-conflation taxonomy already exists and was not used.** The repo distinguishes at least four declaration faces for a grid key (TS interface, zod mirror, published `inputs`/manifest, spec `ComponentPropsMap`), and `title` had a different status on each: declared-deprecated, unmirrored-ledgered, carve-out-by-ruling (#4648), and spec-declared respectively. A census claim that names one face while measuring another reads as true from every seat that checks a different face — which is how this one survived three reviews.

## Suggested direction (not a ruling)

Whoever grades this: re-derive PR #6637's census claims of the form "interface declares no K" against the interface text at the census's own base commit, before any of its remaining cards are dispatched. The fix for the one measured instance is already landed via #6639 / PR #6869; nothing in this card blocks or reopens that work.

Refs: objectui#6639 (the measured instance — stays open/closed on its own PR, not via this card) · PR #6637 (census origin) · objectui#6459 (the mechanism the card borrowed) · objectui#6869 (the correction PR whose body carries the receipt).
